name: South Carolina

regulator.name: South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An NIL contract is an agency contract (S.C. Code 59-102-20). NIL fees are capped at 20%.
summary: Get licensed by the Department of Consumer Affairs. $1,500, good for 2 years. Register before you contact any athlete.
contract_warning:
Warning to student athlete
If you sign this contract:
(1) You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport;
(2) If you have an athletic director, within seventy-two hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and
(3) You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.

steps.text: Apply on the SCDCA online gateway
steps.detail: Paper forms can also be mailed to P.O. Box 5757, Columbia, SC 29250.
$2,500 if based on another state's registration.

steps.text: Don't contact athletes until you're registered
steps.detail: If an athlete contacts you first, apply within 7 days. You still can't sign a contract until you're registered (59-102-40).

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you have someone else contact them. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days (59-102-110).

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you're registered in South Carolina and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed (59-102-100).

steps.text: Put the state's warning in bold capital letters next to the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words in the warning box (59-102-100).

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs if the athlete is a minor (59-102-100).

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too (59-102-110).

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel in writing within 14 days
steps.detail: They can't give up this right (59-102-120).

steps.text: If you signed before the athlete enrolled, tell the new school's athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you knew or should have known they enrolled (59-102-110).

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law (59-102-140) and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Charge no more than 20% on NIL deals
steps.detail: Your pay on an NIL contract can't be more than 20% of the deal. The cap was 10% before 2024 (59-102-100).
Names and addresses of clients, every contract, and what you spent recruiting each athlete (59-102-130).

steps.text: Never give false info or anything of value to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Don't give anything of value to other people to get them to sign either. Federal law (SPARTA) has the same kind of rules (59-102-140).

steps.text: Complete 20 hours of athlete agent education every 2 years
steps.detail: The state can refuse to renew you if you don't (59-102-70).

steps.text: Renew 45 days before your 2 years end and pay $700
steps.detail: $1,000 if based on another state. Late renewals must file as new.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Continuing education: S.C. Code 59-102-70(C) lets SCDCA act if you skip 20 hours every 2 years, but SCDCA's pages don't say which courses count. Ask SCDCA at 803-734-4200.
South Carolina's code site has one page for the whole chapter, so each step names its section in parentheses.
Editor's notes say Act 35 (2021) applies to colleges only as the Attorney General certifies. Confirm with SCDCA that the NIL rules are in effect for your athlete's school.
